required_changes_injected: FAIL — Criterion 2 (Carry-forward consistency): Metrics regressed from 4/10 (cumulative) to 3/10 without documented reason. Identified Pain regressed from 1/10 (unknown) to 4/10 (partial) — this is an upgrade, not a regression, but the analysis must explicitly note the source call data supporting this change. Champion scored 2/10 in new analysis vs. 7/10 in cumulative state — this is a major regression. The cumulative state lists 'Christian identified as the contact person' with score 7/10, but the new analysis downgrades Clemens (not Christian) to 2/10 as champion with reasoning that he has not demonstrated internal selling. The analysis conflates two different people (Christian = sales rep, Clemens = buyer contact) and fails to carry forward the champion assessment. FAIL — Criterion 4 (Actionable next steps): Economic Buyer next step uses '[contact TBD]' placeholder, which is acceptable per rubric exception for early-stage deals, but the next step itself ('Who is the team head...') is acceptable. However, Decision Criteria next step ('Beyond security compliance...') is vague — it asks what other requirements exist but does not specify a concrete action or question format that surfaces a decision blocker. FAIL — Criterion 3 (Evidence quality): Champion section cites evidence 'Clemens demonstrated exceptionally strong champion signals' but then scores him 2/10 for lack of internal selling — this is internally contradictory. The evidence supports a higher score or the score must be justified by different evidence. Identified Pain evidence states 'Neuroth sought to transition from guesswork to data-driven experimentation' but cumulative state scored this 1/10 (unknown). The new analysis upgrades to 4/10 (partial) based on the same call data — this suggests the cumulative state was incorrect, not that new information arrived. Clarify whether this is a re-evaluation of existing data or new call data. FAIL — Criterion 1 (Complete coverage): All components have status and score, but Metrics evidence lacks a direct quote — the statement 'no quantifiable business outcomes were stated' is an absence claim, not evidence from the call. Provide a paraphrase or quote showing what Clemens actually said about success criteria.
